mission: Attack stroke-heuristic-6's generalization without touching held-out cases: replay BOTH v5 (git d6f951f, pre-F20 gates) and current v6 over every replayable committed pose sequence; rank by v5-vs-v6 disagreement and proximity to the two new v6 gates; mine the mission's target geometries; produce a Tier-C annotation queue; measure how often each new gate fires in the wild.
method: Frozen byte-identical v5 replica (packages/swing-lab/src/strokeHeuristicV5Frozen.ts, extracted from commit d6f951f — the last commit before the two v6 gates in 92e0c2c/629a9fc) run side-by-side with current classifyStroke on identical inputs by packages/swing-lab/src/g13H6Mining.ts. Two unit types: (1) all evaluable stroke-gold events (strokeHeuristicBench loading/attribution rules, paddle=null); (2) mined windows — every player track (target AND other) in every committed-pose case, one unit per local maximum of the measured dominant-wrist speed series with >=600ms separation, contactMs=null, eventPeakMs=the measured peak (never a window midpoint). Probe metrics replicate the classifier's internal geometry so gate proximity is measured even where no gate fired.

datasetScope.poseSequences: All 8 committed wave-a people.json runs under datasets/paddle-bench/runs-wave-a/ — the only replayable footage-derived pose in the repo (no other datasets/ path contains people.json; this Linux box cannot extract new pose).
datasetScope.grouping: corpus sessionKey via STROKE_BENCH_POSE_CASES (dvids-marne-2024, afn-sasebo-2025-06, dvids-warriorgames-2026) — never a random frame split.
datasetScope.tier: Mined windows are Tier-C machine proposals (never truth); gold events carry existing stroke-gold labels used only as context, never relabeled.

holdoutStatement: Held-out cases wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 were never read, listed, replayed, or referenced: no people.json path in the repo matches either id (verified by filesystem search returning 0), STROKE_BENCH_POSE_CASES contains neither, and the harness additionally hard-fails if either id ever appears in the case table and skips any gold label naming them.

configuration.inputs: paddle=null, paddleSpeeds=null, wristSpeeds=measured dominantWristSpeeds; handedness from committed bundle annotations (default right when absent)
configuration.minedWindow: peak +/-400ms; peaks = local maxima of wrist-speed series with >=600ms separation, all energies kept

flippedRows: gold:wavea-sasebo-volleys@52434 (v5 BACKHAND 0.60 -> v6 UNKNOWN, sparse gate; gold l1=volley l2=backhand — v5's commit MATCHED gold, so this flip is a measured RECALL COST of the new gate on natural footage: the commit rested on a contradicted arm with the declared wrist glimpsed in 1 frame, i.e. correct possibly by luck, but correct per the only truth available)
mined:wavea-sasebo-volleys:t1@52586 (v5 BACKHAND -> v6 UNKNOWN, sparse gate; same clip/track as the gold flip)
mined:wavea-wgm-wheelchair:t2@183133 (v5 BACKHAND -> v6 UNKNOWN, sparse gate; wheelchair other-track — exactly the ambiguous-arm population the gate targets)

sparse_declared_wrist.note: 4th fire is mined:wavea-944403-smash:t6@3153 where v5 ALSO abstained (different downstream reason) — label unchanged, reason changed.
sparse_declared_wrist.armedNote: 19/118 units measure a non-decisive handedness contradiction with declared-wrist frames <5 (the gate's geometric precondition); 15 of those abstain EARLIER in both versions (rival-unmeasured, non-swing, side-margin, facing gates), so the new gate is the deciding factor in only 4. It fires at a moderate, plausible rate — evidence it is live, not dead and not a fire-always trap.
sparse_declared_wrist.nearMisses: 3 further units sit just above the floor (rival measured 5-6 frames) — prime annotation targets for threshold sensitivity.

median_normalization.preconditionCounts: Only 1/118 units even has its wrist-derived contact above the 0.25 overhead line under reference normalization (gold:wavea-944403-smash@3617, ratio ref/median 1.02 — honest normalization, no compression, and it stays OVERHEAD in both versions); 0/118 satisfy the gate's arming condition (raised point AND reference extent < sequence median).
median_normalization.interpretation: The gate NEVER fires in the wild on this corpus. That is evidence of a narrow target: with paddle=null the contact point is the dominant wrist, and wrist-height-above-0.25-torso at reference normalization is itself rare (1/118). F20-F2 remains covered only by its redteam fixture; no natural dev example of the partial-torso-compression overhead exists in committed pose. Real coverage needs either paddle-tracked overheads or footage with genuinely compressed torsos at contact — queued categories torso_collapse (2) and partial_torso_compression (5) are the closest natural candidates.

measuredResults.categoryNotes: wrong_arm_geometry (dominant-motion wrist opposite the declared hand) occurs in 56/118 units — far more common in the wild than the redteam fixtures suggested, dominated by far-court/other-player tracks with sparse wrists. serve_return_raised_arm needs gold serve/return labels with raised-arm geometry; the only serve gold (wavea-marne-serve) measured no raised frames at its reference. occluded_or_cropped_torso (>=30% window frames missing a torso joint) never occurs because buildPlayerTracks only emits frames with full torsos — torso cropping manifests upstream as missing FRAMES, which this probe cannot see; disclosed as a mining blind spot.

annotationQueue.ranking: infoScore = disagreement severity (v6-new-gate flip highest) + proximity to both v6 gate thresholds + category richness + gold-context bonus; top 3 are the three v5->v6 flips.

findings: The sparse-declared-wrist gate (F20-F1) is LIVE in the wild: 4/118 fires, 3 of which flip a v5 side-commit to abstention. The only flip with gold coverage (wavea-sasebo-volleys@52434, gold volley/backhand) abstained on a commit that MATCHED gold: on measured dev data the gate's net effect so far is -1 correct commit / 0 wrong commits prevented (its benefit exists only in the F20-F1 redteam fixture). Whether the two unlabeled mined flips were wrong commits is exactly what the queue's top entries ask a human to decide.

The median-normalization overhead cross-check (F20-F2) NEVER fires (0/118) and its arming precondition never occurs (0/118); only 1/118 units even crosses the overhead line. On committed dev pose the gate is inert — untested by nature, not validated by it.

Wrong-arm geometry is endemic (56/118), but 15/19 of the sparse-gate-armed units are already caught by earlier gates in BOTH versions — v6's marginal effect is small and surgical (3 label flips, 0 regressions, no v5-abstain->v6-commit and no committed-label mismatches anywhere).
Mining blind spot disclosed: torso cropping/occlusion cannot be observed by this harness because the track builder drops torso-less frames before the classifier ever sees them.
No unit anywhere in 118 measured a v6 behavior WORSE than v5 (no new commits, no label changes among commits).
verdictRationale: Honest split result. Gate 11 (sparse declared wrist): fires at a live, surgical rate (4/118) but its ONLY gold-covered wild fire abstained on a commit that matched gold — measured wild net effect is a recall cost (-1 correct commit, 0 wrong commits prevented); its benefit is so far fixture-only. Gate 12 (median normalization): zero wild evidence — never armed on 118 units of committed dev pose, so its generalization is UNTESTED outside its fixture; anyone claiming it 'works in the wild' would be fabricating. Not RED: no confidently-wrong prediction was introduced anywhere (no new commits, no label changes among commits) and one gold flip is far too small an n to condemn the gate. Not GREEN: neither gate has a measured wild win. The 76-entry Tier-C queue (top-ranked: the 3 flips, 3 sparse-gate near-misses, torso-compression and near-profile extremes) is the produced instrument for turning this YELLOW into truth via human labels.
